meta.protocol: Sampler, author and compiler are separate. The author saw five fields of one anchor -- name, kind, the relationship it holds, the direction, and whether the question should ask for a technique, a mitigation, or nothing of the sort -- and NEVER the expected answer, the declared correspondence, the schema, or another question. Gold was computed from the generator blueprint and the declared edge->technique map before any question text existed, with the ATT&CK side read from the canonical export rather than the live store. Audited: 0 of 73 questions contain any gold identifier, 73 of 73 name their anchor, 0 use SCREAMING_CASE relationship names, and 0 identity-control questions mention ATT&CK.
meta.limit: The edge->technique mapping is authored by us. A score against this bank measures whether the system USES the declared bridge correctly, not whether the mapping is right.
meta.note_partial_control: A `bridge-partial` control -- an anchor holding ONE half of the DCSync right pair -- is NOT in this bank. It is not drawable from this tenant: every anchor holding GET_CHANGES is also touched by another mapped right, usually ALL_EXTENDED_RIGHTS, which the declaration maps to T1003.006 in its own right on the customer's wording that it includes 'on a domain, the replication rights'. A T1003.006 in the evidence therefore cannot be attributed to the half-right rather than the whole one, so the control cannot distinguish the behaviour it exists to test. Testing it needs a tenant generated with an isolated replication right, which is a separate experiment.
meta.note_negative_anchors: Negative-control anchors are clean in BOTH directions. The first draw indexed outgoing edges only, and the runtime walk is direction-agnostic, so `dc202` was selected as a refusal control on its lone outgoing RUNS_AS and then correctly produced T1098 from a WRITE_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTIONS edge held OVER it. Scored naively that reads as the bridge inventing a technique. The declaration was right, the system was right, and the gold was wrong.
